architecture_constraints: Canonical namespace target is supp.* (never suppl.*).
Knowledge/research staging only; not Patient/Case/Visit data.
No supplement observation auto-creates TCM disease or pattern.
Ingredient identity stays separate from commercial product/brand identity.
No canonical promotion before template, ID rules, taxonomy, ingestion contract and validators are locked.
Safety/interaction fields must be source-backed and distinguish unknown/not-reviewed from reviewed-and-none-found.
Clinical exposure recording references supp.* through the existing snapshot + append-only event model.
taxonomy_findings: Most candidates fit the current 8 categories.
Glucosamine and chondroitin do not fit naturally.
Resolve taxonomy gaps before bulk generation.

NIH_ODS.name: NIH Office of Dietary Supplements — Dietary Supplement Fact Sheets
NIH_ODS.use: Primary federal source for ingredient identity, intake/safety context, and medication-interaction sections when an ingredient fact sheet exists.

NIH_ODS_VITMIN.name: NIH ODS — Vitamin and Mineral Supplement Fact Sheets
NIH_ODS_VITMIN.use: Primary federal source map for vitamins and minerals.

NIH_ODS_BOTANICAL.name: NIH ODS — Botanical Supplement Fact Sheets
NIH_ODS_BOTANICAL.use: Federal source directory for botanicals, frequently routing to NCCIH.

NCCIH.name: NIH NCCIH — Dietary and Herbal Supplements
NCCIH.use: Primary federal source for botanical/supplement safety, evidence summaries, and interaction cautions.

FDA_SUPP.name: U.S. FDA — Dietary Supplements
FDA_SUPP.use: Regulatory/safety layer; FDA does not pre-approve supplements for safety/effectiveness. Use for alerts, unlawful ingredients, and post-market safety actions.

FDA_INGREDIENT_ALERTS.name: U.S. FDA — Information on Select Dietary Supplement Ingredients and Other Substances
FDA_INGREDIENT_ALERTS.use: Safety/enforcement lookup for selected ingredients and substances.
